note: Myanmar flood data. UNOSAT flood extents are a hand-converted snapshot (see scripts/convert_unosat.py); the impact figures are refreshed automatically by scripts/scan_adam.py. This file was previously data/extra-index.json, kept separate because the NIED scanner rewrote index.json on every run — that scanner is gone, so it is now the primary index.

datasets.name: Yangon Region, Myanmar
datasets.note: Sentinel-1, 31 Aug 2021 (UNOSAT FL20210831MMR). The analysis extent barely reaches Yangon Region, so almost no flood water is mapped here — this is a gap in the imagery analysed, not evidence that the region stayed dry. The water layer is the same sensor and date as the flood layer (Sentinel-1, 2021-08-31). Two Sentinel-1 passes are published for this event: 2021-08-25 and 2021-08-31. Both are included, so the earlier layer showing through the later one is water that had drained in those six days.

stats.label: Flood risk share
stats.source: supplied to the project; provenance not established. The four shares are exactly 16/9/4/1 of 30 records, so this is a tally, not a modelled probability.

datasets.name: Mandalay Region, Myanmar
datasets.note: Sentinel-1, 24 Sep 2024, Typhoon Yagi (UNOSAT FL20240912MMR). Nay Pyi Taw Union Territory is excluded — geoBoundaries ADM1 still draws it inside Mandalay Region, which would double-count it. Note: the water layer for this region comes from Gaofen-3 imaged 2024-09-15, a different satellite and nine days earlier than the flood layer (Sentinel-1, 2024-09-24) — UNOSAT published no Sentinel-1 water extent for this event. Treat the two as separate observations, not a before/after pair.

datasets.name: Myanmar — nationwide flood exposure
datasets.note: AI-detected surface water from Sentinel-1, observed 2026-08-08, covering the whole country — 207 townships with an observation. Radar underestimates water under dense vegetation and in built-up areas, and the population figures are modelled from WorldPop, which can overestimate in cities. Preliminary, not field-validated.
